analysis.investment_thesis: KRN is a genuinely impressive small-cap business — 40% revenue CAGR, expanding margins, near debt-free — but the market has already discovered it and priced in a decade of growth at 116x P/E and ₹7,893 Cr market cap, which is 8x outside my sweet spot. At this price, the multibagger thesis is dead on arrival.
key_strengths: Exceptional growth trajectory — revenue CAGR 40.2%, net profit CAGR 71.1% over 3 years with margins expanding from 10% to 16.5%
Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.06) with ₹528 Cr equity post-IPO; promoter skin in game at 70.79%
Structural tailwind — HVAC/refrigeration demand driven by India urbanization, rising AC penetration, and cold chain growth; global exports to Europe/North America add quality credibility
key_risks: Valuation is extreme — P/E 116x, EV/EBITDA 85.7x, P/S 14.3x on ₹430 Cr revenue; even forward P/E of 58x leaves no margin of safety
Deeply negative FCF (-₹65 Cr in 2025) driven by aggressive ₹151 Cr capex; OCF only ₹21 Cr on ₹430 Cr revenue — capital intensity is high
Incorporated only in 2017 — no track record through a full economic cycle; customer concentration (OEM-dependent) creates revenue cliff risk
red_flags: Market cap ₹7,893 Cr — 8x outside my 100-1,000 Cr sweet spot; institutional discovery is complete
P/E 116x vs my preferred 8-15x entry — price already embeds 15-20 years of perfect execution
IPO-inflated equity (₹130 Cr → ₹528 Cr in one year) and ₹258 Cr financing CF suggest the easy re-rating is done
analysis.detailed_analysis:
KRN's operating story is clean and compelling. Revenue grew from ₹156 Cr to ₹430 Cr in 3 years (40% CAGR), operating margins expanded from 10.3% to 16.3%, EBITDA CAGR hit 63.5%, and the balance sheet is essentially debt-free at D/E 0.06 post-IPO. The HVAC/refrigeration components market is a genuine structural play on India's cooling demand, and the company's export reach across Europe and North America signals product quality. Promoter holding at 70.79% is excellent. On pure business quality, this would score 7-8 out of 10.

But as Vijay Kedia, I invest in discovery, not confirmation. At ₹7,893 Cr market cap and 116x earnings, every analyst and FII (already at 6.66%) knows this story. The P/E is 7-8x my maximum comfort level, and the deeply negative FCF (-₹65 Cr) despite strong earnings means the business is consuming cash at precisely the moment when the stock demands perfection. I would revisit seriously if market cap corrects to ₹800-1,500 Cr range — but that would require an 80-90% price drop, which tells you how stretched the current multiple truly is.
